questions.question: Comprehension:Read the passage carefully and answer the questions that follow. By mid-2025, the global water crisis is expected to reach unprecedented levels. According to the 2024 UN World Water Development Report, approximately 2.2 billion people lack access to safely managed drinking water, and 3.5 billion lack safely managed sanitation services. Meanwhile, nearly half of the world’s population experiences severe water scarcity for at least part of each year. Agriculture consumes about 70% of global freshwater withdrawals, while industry and municipal use account for roughly 20% and 12%, respectively. Climate change is further destabilizing the hydrological cycle. Rising temperatures, glacial melt, and changing precipitation patterns are reducing freshwater availability, while floods and droughts increase in frequency and severity. Coastal aquifers face growing salinization: studies show that by 2100, as much as 77% of coastal aquifers could be affected by saltwater intrusion due to sea-level rise and declining recharge. Water scarcity today already affects 40% of the global population, and demand is expected to surpass supply by 40% by 2030. Groundwater depletion continues, especially in densely populated regions like India, China, and Pakistan, where aquifer recharge lags behind extraction. Many megacities now face “Day Zero” scenarios, where municipal taps could run dry without drastic conservation and infrastructure reform. While innovative technologies—such as biodegradable hydrogels that extract water from the air—offer promise for remote or water-stressed regions, current investments fall significantly short of what's needed (a shortfall of $85 billion per year) to achieve universal access by 2030. Experts warn that without coordinated global investment, transparent governance, equitable distribution, and water-efficient infrastructure, the world risks escalating conflict, agricultural collapse, economic instability, and public health crises on a global scale.What is the central theme of the passage?
options: Rising water scarcity driven by climate and mismanagement
questions.explanation: सही उत्तर विकल्प 'D' (Rising water scarcity driven by climate and mismanagement) है।

questions.question: Comprehension:Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow. Mutual fund investment is a widely used financial instrument that pools money from multiple investors to invest in diversified portfolios of stocks, bonds, or other securities. This approach enables investors to benefit from professional fund management while minimising risk through diversification. Mutual funds are categorised into various types, such as equity funds, debt funds, hybrid funds, and index funds, each catering to different investment objectives and risk appetites. One of the primary advantages of mutual funds is liquidity. Investors can enter or exit their investments at prevailing Net Asset Value (NAV), making them a flexible investment choice. Another advantage is accessibility—mutual funds allow small investors to participate in capital markets without requiring extensive financial expertise. Additionally, systematic investment plans (SIPs) help investors develop financial discipline by investing small amounts regularly rather than making lump sum contributions. However, mutual fund investments also come with inherent risks. Market fluctuations, interest rate variations, and economic downturns can impact returns. Actively managed funds depend on fund managers' skills, and their expense ratios may be higher compared to passively managed index funds. Additionally, exit loads and tax implications can influence an investor's final returns. A key consideration when investing in mutual funds is aligning one’s financial goals with the fund’s objectives. For instance, aggressive investors with a long-term horizon may opt for equity funds, while conservative investors may prefer debt funds for stability. Understanding risk-return trade-offs, evaluating historical fund performance, and considering the expense ratio are crucial steps in making informed investment decisions. Thus, while mutual funds offer a structured way to invest in the financial markets, their success depends on an investor’s ability to analyse, adapt, and align their investments with broader financial strategies.Q80. Select the most appropriate title of the passage.
options: "Why Mutual Funds Are the Best Investment Choice"
"Understanding Mutual Funds: Balancing Risk and Reward"
questions.explanation: सही उत्तर विकल्प 'D' ("Understanding Mutual Funds: Balancing Risk and Reward") है।

Comprehension:Read the given passage carefully and answer the questions that follow.The multiplicity of our languages and communities is widely advertised, but little emphasis is laid on certain facts which make India what she is. Throughout the last two millennia, there was linguistic unity. Some sort of a lingua franca was used by a very large part of the country; and Sanskrit, for a thousand years the language of royal courts and at all times the language of culture, was predominant, influencing life, language, and literature in most provinces. For over three thousand years, social and family life had been moulded or influenced by the Dharma-Shastra texts, containing a comprehensive code of personal law, which, though adapted from time to time to suit every age and province, provided a continuous unifying social force. Aryan, or rather the Hindu culture (for there was considerable Dravidian influence) drew its inspiration in every successive generation from Sanskrit works on religion, philosophy, ritual, law, and science, and particularly the two epics, the Mahabharata and Ramayana, and the Bhagavata, underwent recensions from time to time, and became the one irresistible creative force which has shaped the collective spirit of the people. Age after age, the best of Indians, from the mythical Vasishtha to the modem Gandhiji, found self-fulfilment in living up to an ideal of conduct in accordance with a code of life, which may be traced back as far as the Upanishads.Identify the most suitable title for the passage.
options: The Unifying Forces Shaping Indian Identity
The Lingua Franca of Ancient India
questions.explanation: सही उत्तर विकल्प 'A' (The Unifying Forces Shaping Indian Identity) है।

Comprehension:Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow.In the age of algorithmic decision-making, predictive governance has emerged as a dominant paradigm for public administration. Governments are increasingly deploying data-driven models to pre-empt criminal activity, optimise urban planning, and forecast economic volatility. While ostensibly rational, this model introduces a paradox: the more predictive power a system accumulates, the more it flattens human agency into statistical probabilities. The future becomes not an open horizon but a quantifiable extension of past behaviours. This techno-bureaucratic reliance risks marginalising outliers — those whose experiences fall outside normative data sets — and institutionalising bias under the guise of objectivity. Moreover, the ethical oversight of such systems lags far behind their deployment, creating a governance vacuum wherein accountability is outsourced to opaque algorithms. In prioritising efficiency and foresight, predictive governance often bypasses deliberative democracy, weakening participatory channels in favour of streamlined outcomes.Citizens are recast as data points, their individual complexities reduced to patterns in a machine-readable format. This mechanistic interpretation of society may inadvertently erode trust in institutions that no longer appear responsive but merely anticipatory. Therefore, the question is not only whether predictive systems function but also for whom they function — and who is excluded by their logic. A governance structure that projects authority through prediction must be tempered by transparent frameworks, ethical scrutiny, and above all, a reaffirmation of the human condition as more than a predictable variable.What is the central theme of the passage?
options: The superiority of algorithmic decision-making in policy
The ethical and democratic implications of data-driven governance
The future of AI in economics
The technical limitations of predictive models
questions.explanation: सही उत्तर विकल्प 'B' (The ethical and democratic implications of data-driven governance) है।

Comprehension:Read the passage and answer the questions: The Solar System consists of the Sun and all the objects bound to it by gravity, including eight planets, their moons, and other celestial bodies like dwarf planets, comets, and asteroids. The Sun, a medium-sized star, is the centre of the Solar System and contains about 99.8% of its total mass. Its gravitational pull keeps the planets in orbit.The planets are divided into two categories: terrestrial planets and gas giants. The terrestrial planets—Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars—are rocky and have solid surfaces. The gas giants—Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune—are much larger and composed mostly of hydrogen and helium. Each planet has unique characteristics; for example, Earth is the only planet known to support life, while Jupiter is the largest planet in the Solar System with a prominent system of rings and moons.In addition to planets, the Solar System is home to many other objects. The asteroid belt, located between Mars and Jupiter, contains numerous rocky bodies. Beyond Neptune lies the Kuiper Belt, a region filled with icy bodies and dwarf planets like Pluto. Comets, which originate from the Kuiper Belt and the distant Oort Cloud, are made of ice and dust and develop spectacular tails when they approach the Sun.Understanding the Solar System helps scientists learn about the formation and evolution of planetary systems, the potential for life elsewhere in the universe, and the dynamics of celestial bodies. The exploration of the Solar System is ongoing, with missions such as the Mars rovers and the Voyager spacecraft providing valuable data about our cosmic neighborhood.Which of the following are terrestrial planets?

questions.question: Comprehension:दिए गए गद्यांंश के आधार पर निम्नांकित प्रश्नों के उत्तर दीजिए-एक बस्ती में दो विद्वान रहते थे, जिनके विचारों में अत्यधिक मतभेद था और वे सदा एक – दूसरे की योग्यता पर व्यंग्य करते थे। उनमें से एक नास्तिक था और दूसरा आस्तिक।एक दिन दोनों बाजार में मिले और अपने – अपने अनुयोयियों की उपस्थिति में भगवान के अस्तित्व पर वाद – विवाद करने लगे। घंटों वाद – विवाद करने के पश्चात वे एक – दूसरे से अलग हुए।उसी साँझ नास्तिक मंदिर में गया और अपने पूर्वपापों के लिए भगवान से क्षमा – याचना करने लगा। दूसरे विद्वान ने घर जाकर अपनी सब धार्मिक पुस्तकें जला दीं; क्योंकि अब वह एक नास्तिक बन चुका था।किसकी उपस्थिति में दोनों विद्वान ईश्वर के अस्तित्व पर वाद – विवाद करते थे ?

Comprehension:नोट: गद्यांश के आधार पर अग्रलिखित प्रश्नों के उत्तर दीजिए।प्राचीन जनजातीय समाजों में बहुपति व्यवस्था भी पाई जाती थी। जिसमें पुनः स्त्री को केन्द्रीय स्थान प्राप्त था। इस प्रकार विस्तार में देखा जाए तो मातृसत्तात्मक परिवार, वधुमूल्य, घोटुल, विवाह, पुनर्विवाह और तलाक में स्त्री अधिकारों का होना और सबसे प्रमुख स्त्री की उर्वरा शक्ति को प्रकृति की उर्वरा शक्ति से जोड़कर देखना एक बहुत प्राचीन भारतीय भौतिकवादी दर्शन की तरफ इशारा करता है। इसे लोकायत दर्शन कहा गया है और इसकी परिभाषा “लोकेषु आयत:” के रूप में की गयी है। अर्थात लोक का दर्शन या इस लोक का दर्शन जिसमें प्रकृति और उसकी शक्तियों को सर्वोपरि माना जाता है। शंकराचार्य ने भी लोकायत को ‘प्राकृत जना:’ का दर्शन माना है और इसे हीन दर्शन या भौतिकवादियों का दर्शन बताया है। इस दर्शन में कृषि से जुड़े कर्मकांडों में स्त्री की भूमिका बहुत महत्त्वपूर्ण मानी गयी थी। इसीलिए प्राचीन जनजातियों में ग्राम देवियों सहित वन देवियों की मान्यता बहुत अधिक पायी जाती है। डॉ. आंबेडकर ने भी अपनी रिसर्च में ये सवाल खड़े किये हैं कि भारत में देवियों और मातृदेवियों का उभार एक गहन पहेली है जिसके आधार पर इस देश के धर्म-दर्शन के उद्भव एवं विकास के बहुत सारे पहलू उजागर किये जा सकते हैं।637जनजातीय समाज में स्त्री की उर्वरा शक्ति को किस से जोड़कर देखा जाता है-640

questions.question: Comprehension:गद्यांश के आधार पर प्रश्न का उत्तर दें।​​​​​​​भूषण शिवाजी के समकालीन थे और उन्होंने शिवाजी तथा छत्रसाल दोनों का आश्रय ग्रहण किया। शिवराज भूषण, शिवा बावनी और छत्रसाल दशक इनके प्रसिद्ध ग्रंथ हैं। रीतिकाल की सर्वाधिक लोकप्रिय काव्य- प्रवृत्ति – श्रृंगारिकता की उपेक्षा करते हुए इन्होंने अपने प्रसिद्ध अलंकार-निरुपक ग्रंथ ‘शिवराज भूषण’ में वीर प्रशस्तिपरक उदाहरणों की रचना की है। इनके दो मुक्तक ग्रंथ ‘शिवा बावनी’ और ‘छत्रसाल दशक’ में इनका कवि रूप अधिक उभर सका है। वीर रस के साथ-साथ अद्भुत, भयानक, वीभत्स और रौद्र भी इसमें व्यंजित हुए हैं। भूषण की सभी रचनाएँ मुक्तक हैं। इनकी साहित्यिक भाषा ब्रज है। ‘भूषण’ वास्तव में इनका नाम नहीं बल्कि उपाधि है जो इन्हें चित्रकूट के नरेश सोलंकी हृदयराम के पुत्र रूद्र ने प्रदान की थी। भूषण की कविता में ओज है। वह वीर रस के कवि थे। ओज ने उनकी कविता में आवेग को भरा। यह आवेग उन्हें सामाजिक जीवन से मिला था। सामाजिक जीवन की परिस्थिति की माँग युद्ध और आक्रमण था। युद्ध और आक्रमण की कविता के लिए जिस प्रकार से भाव का संगठन काव्य में होना चाहिए उसी प्रकार का भाव भूषण की कविता में मिलता है। भूषण की कविता में आवेग और अनुभूति की एकता है।194निम्न में से भूषण की रचना नहीं है--196
